metadata.epic6_memory_canonical_attribution: Traced current and peak values cover the complete guarded canonical dispatch boundary. They are not attributed to Registry projection or any individual request component.
metadata.epic6_memory_canonical_limitation: Canonical results remain placeholders until the guarded PostgreSQL benchmark test profiles the full inclusive dispatch boundary.
metadata.epic6_memory_canonical_trial_method: Three independent isolated PostgreSQL fixtures with 100 active visible datasets. Each dataset-list call is traced once per fixture with DEBUG=False, performance instrumentation disabled, and no SQL or latency capture. The boundary includes canonical dispatch, authorization, database access, and result projection.

epic6_memory_decision.rationale: The benchmark distinguishes temporary Python-traced allocations from signed post-GC retention deltas. Direct results are projection-only, while canonical results are inclusive dispatch measurements and are not attributed to projection.

metadata.epic6_memory_trial_method: Three independent traced trials per single, repeated, and concurrent scenario. Inputs are prepared before each tracing boundary; returned output strings remain alive for current/peak readings and are released before GC.
metadata.methodology: RR-09.2 profiles Python allocations with isolated tracemalloc boundaries. It is separate from RR-09.1 latency, SQL, and performance-event evidence.
